Clyde Kerr Jr. was born in New Orleans on July 27, 1943. He has taught and mentored numerous young musicians who now carry on the legacy of New Orleans music. Clyde’s trumpet can be heard on many jazz and R&B recordings and he speaks fondly of his performances with friends Alvin “Red” Tyler and Kidd Jordan.
Clyde was interviewed in Rome, New York on August 22, 2006 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
My name is Monk Rowe and we are filming in Rome, New York for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. It’s a pleasure for me to have Clyde Kerr Jr. with me today.
I’m glad you’re up here in the north. I found it interesting that most of you have been commenting on the nice weather.
Oh yeah man. We won’t see this type of weather in New Orleans, maybe not until January.

No we don’t have the seasons like a long time ago man. Right now it’s very hot and humid and it’s raining quite a bit and it’s making it crazy and everybody’s eyes are on the skies. Hurricane season you know.

So yeah it is a pleasure to be up here man. If anything were going to happen, let it happen now while I’m up here, I’m already evacuated. I don’t wish that to happen ever again in my lifetime or anybody else.
You feel like talking about that a little bit?
